general_information.Description: This course addresses the comprehension and application of Digital Forensic Investigations. Students will evaluate and synthesize technical and legal issues in relation to digital evidence. Students will apply various skills and techniques, combined with numerous investigative software tools to analyze seized electronic media. Students subject to background investigation prior to admittance. Assessment scheme: 1) On-going Assessment - 01 Midterm Progress Test: 20% - Participation in Discussions: 10% - 14 Lab-Projects: 40% 2) 01 Final Exam: 30% 3) Final Result 100% Completion Criteria: 1) Every on-going assessment component >0 2) Average Lab Score >= 4 3) Final Exam Score >=4 & Final Result >=5
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit in time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FPTU LMS at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Defining Digital Forensics and examining how it’s being used.
Understanding how computers create and store digital information is a perquisite for the study of digital forensics.
Examining digital forensic environment, hardware and software, and standards used on a regular basis, to accredit labs and validate tools.
Collecting digital evidence, establishing a chain of custody, and understanding its major role when admitted into court.
Understanding many of the common Windows artifacts and how they are created.
Examining tools and techniques used to hide or destroy data with the aim to recover digital evidence, deleted files, and the like.
Explaining the legal aspects of digital forensics in searching.
Understanding social networks, e-mail, chat logs, and Internet history representing some of the best evidence.
Understanding how networks are attacked and what role digital forensics plays in not only the response, but in how perpetrators can be traced.
Understanding the underlying technology powering cell phones and GPS units, as well as the potential evidence they could contain.

assessments.Grading Guide: Guided by instructor - 14 Lab-Projects are arranged relevant to the chapter theory - Student must finish labs and submit the results to the lecturer in class. - An average point of all labs could be evaluated and published to students at the end of the semester.

The test must be taken right after the last lectures of required material. Instructor has responsibility to review the test for students after graded.
